> **What this case shows** — how conscious you are leaves a fingerprint in how *complex*
> your cortex's activity is. **Lempel-Ziv complexity** — how compressible a signal is, its
> information content — is the basis of the **Perturbational Complexity Index**, a
> validated index of the *level* of consciousness. It should therefore fall as
> consciousness fades into deep sleep and recover in dreaming. On a real overnight EEG it
> does exactly that: LZ complexity is **0.464 in wake**, dips to **0.420 in N2**, reaches
> its **minimum of 0.364 in deep (N3) sleep**, and climbs back to **0.464 in REM** — the
> dreaming stage, as complex as wake. Because Lempel-Ziv is an *exactly-defined*
> algorithm, the ecosystem's `eegComplexity` reproduces the canonical Python **antropy**
> to **machine precision** across all four stages (max |diff| = 5.6×10⁻¹⁷).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for signal complexity: `eegComplexity(pe, measures = "lempel_ziv")` → read
the per-channel LZ → compare it across conditions (stages, groups, arousal levels).
**Way of thinking** — complexity is a *level*, not a rhythm: a highly compressible
(regular, low-LZ) EEG is the signature of reduced consciousness; a rich, incompressible
(high-LZ) EEG is wake-like. To compare LZ across conditions, keep the signals the same
length — the normalization is length-dependent.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::eegComplexity()` offers Lempel-Ziv alongside
permutation / sample / multiscale entropy, DFA, Hjorth and spectral entropy.
:::

## Proposition

On a real overnight EEG (Sleep-EDF SC4001, Fpz-Cz), Lempel-Ziv complexity is lowest in
deep sleep (N3 = 0.364) and highest in wake and REM (0.464) — the consciousness gradient
— and `eegComplexity`'s LZ reproduces `antropy.lziv_complexity` to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is whether cortical complexity tracks consciousness — and whether the
ecosystem computes it correctly.** LZ complexity is only useful as a consciousness index
if the number is right and comparable. The goal is two-fold: recover the established
sleep gradient (LZ lowest in deep sleep) and validate the LZ computation against the
canonical `antropy`.

## Challenge & approach

LZ complexity is length-dependent, so to compare stages we take the *same length* (60 s)
of EEG from each stage, compute LZ with `eegComplexity`, and check the gradient; the
deep-sleep value is validated, per stage, against `antropy.lziv_complexity`.

```
overnight EEG + hypnogram → 60 s per stage (Wake / N2 / N3 / REM)
                          → eegComplexity(lempel_ziv)  (== antropy.lziv_complexity)
                          → LZ gradient: N3 lowest
```

## Data

**Sleep-EDF Expanded (sleep-edfx, PhysioNet)**: subject SC4001, overnight PSG. EEG
**Fpz-Cz** at 100 Hz; a 60-s fixed-length concatenation per stage, grouped from the
expert hypnogram (the same PSG the `netphys-sleep` and `pac-sleep` cases read). Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: Lempel-Ziv complexity by sleep stage — high in wake and REM (0.464), intermediate in N2 (0.420), lowest in deep N3 sleep (0.364); complexity falls as consciousness fades and recovers in dreaming (REM). Right: a 10-s EEG trace of wake (red) versus deep sleep N3 (blue) — N3's slow, regular high-amplitude waves are more compressible (lower LZ).](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* a lower bar means a more *compressible*, regular EEG — the signature
of reduced consciousness. Deep sleep (N3) is the minimum; REM, the dreaming stage, is back
up at wake level.

| Stage | LZ complexity | vs antropy |
|---|---|---|
| Wake | **0.464** | matches (\|diff\| < 1e-16) |
| REM | **0.464** | matches |
| N2 | **0.420** | matches |
| N3 (deep) | **0.364** | matches |

The complexity gradient is clear (wake − N3 = 0.100), and every stage matches `antropy` to
machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/lz_summary.csv`](artifacts/lz_summary.csv) and the per-stage table
[`artifacts/lz_by_stage.csv`](artifacts/lz_by_stage.csv).

## Conclusion

Cortical complexity fades in deep sleep and returns in dreaming, and the ecosystem measures
that consciousness signature with an operator that is exactly the field-standard `antropy`.
The transferable takeaway: **use Lempel-Ziv complexity as a level-of-consciousness index —
an exactly-defined measure you can validate to the bit — and compare it across
equal-length signals, because its normalization depends on length.**

## Open questions

- The gradient is the signature: tracking LZ complexity **continuously across a whole
  night** (does it dip with each deep-sleep cycle?), **across subjects**, or against an
  **anaesthesia depth** would turn this validated estimator into a consciousness-monitoring
  study — the **Perturbational Complexity Index** applies the same idea to TMS-evoked
  responses to score consciousness in coma and disorders of consciousness (see the
  [tms-eeg case](../tms-eeg-tep-tesa/)). A multi-channel **spatiotemporal** LZ would extend
  it further. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Lempel-Ziv (and other) complexity | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |
| permutation entropy (predictability) | `eegComplexity(measures="permutation_entropy")` | PhysioEEG |
| the aperiodic 1/f background (state) | `eegAperiodic()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **measure** — `"lempel_ziv"` for information content / consciousness level; it is
  exactly defined and reproducible. Pair it with `"permutation_entropy"` (predictability)
  for a complementary view.
- **equal length** — compare LZ only across **equal-length** signals; the normalization
  (÷ log₂(n)/n) is length-dependent, so unequal windows bias the comparison.
- **binarization** — LZ binarizes the signal (here at the median); keep the same rule
  across conditions.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

cx <- eegComplexity(pe, measures = "lempel_ziv")     # per-channel LZ
cx$lempel_ziv                                         # 0.364 in deep sleep, 0.464 in wake

# exact by construction: matches antropy.lziv_complexity (median-binarized, normalized)
# to machine precision.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/`](artifacts/) — the summary in
[`lz_summary.csv`](artifacts/lz_summary.csv) and the per-stage table (with antropy
alongside) in [`lz_by_stage.csv`](artifacts/lz_by_stage.csv) — and [`audit.py`](audit.py)
re-checks each reported number, the machine-precision `antropy` agreement on every stage,
and the deep-sleep complexity minimum.
